subject: Keystone VM evidence, remediation timeline, and signed attestation
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finserv.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finserv.com
Date: Sat, 30 Aug 2025 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: Keystone VM evidence and remediation attestation

Hi Camila,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG review and SOC 2 audit, we need a compact evidence packet for your Keystone service covering: scan cadence, recent finding summary, and attestations for remediation of two high CVEs we flagged in our discovery: CVE-2025-3397 and CVE-2025-7841. Our audit window is tight — could you get a formal attestation and the supporting artifacts over by end-of-day Monday (US/PST)?

Specifically we need:
- A one-page attestation that lists the CVEs and their remediation windows (dates + owners).
- Scan artifacts (summary of results and minimal CSV with findings).
- The playbook or runbook you used to triage and patch; if there are any compensating controls in place, note them.

Also please confirm whether you observed any active exploitation or evidence of lateral movement tied to those CVEs.

If we can get a signed PDF (DocuSign OK) that will help expedite the SIG submission.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen | Security Lead, Finserv Systems

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finserv.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 30 Aug 2025 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: Keystone VM evidence and remediation attestation

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a compact packet that should cover the SIG/SOC2 reviewers. Highlights below and attachments are included: keystone-scan-summary-2025Q2.csv, vm-ops-playbook-2025.pdf, and cve-closure-attestation-keystone-2025-08.pdf.

Quick summary:
- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated SAST/DAST for application components, weekly unauthenticated network scans, monthly external/edge scans, quarterly third-party pentest. We retain scan artifacts for 24 months.
- Remediation SLA we operate to (severity-based):
  - Critical (CVE with exploitability and active impact): 48 hours to mitigation plan, 7 days to fix or approved exception.
  - High: 72 hours to mitigation plan, 30 days to remediation.
  - Medium/Low: 90/180 days respectively depending on risk.
- CVE specifics:
  - CVE-2025-3397 (Keystone auth token handling) — issue detected in our 2025-07-21 SAST run, JIRA INF-4821 opened 2025-07-22, mitigation deployed 2025-07-29 (backported hotfix + config lock). Evidence: INF-4821 ticket export included in the CSV row. No signs of exploitation in logs for the affected time window.
  - CVE-2025-7841 (third-party library deserialization) — identified 2025-06-15, patch applied 2025-06-30 with further runtime hardening (sandboxing) 2025-07-02. Proof in the attestation PDF.

Irene (cc) has reviewed the attestation language for legal/contract acceptability. If you need a signed DocuSign envelope, we can issue it — see link in follow-up.

On observed exploitation: we have not found confirmed exploitation traces for either CVE. We ran targeted log searches (auth logs, EDR telemetry) for the relevant host ranges and behavioral indicators; summary included in the CSV. If your team wants raw logs we can provide an export under an NDA channel, but for SIG we typically submit the attached artifacts.

Let me know if you want tighter SLA commitments for the account — we can propose a cadence amendment if Finserv requires an accelerated SLA beyond our standard.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Security Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finserv.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Michael Liu <michael.liu@auditco.com>, security@finserv.com
Date: Sun, 31 Aug 2025 09:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: Keystone VM evidence and remediation attestation

Camila — this is great, thanks for the fast turn. A couple quick follow-ups before we route to SIG:
- Can you include a short line that explicitly states “no evidence of exploitation observed”? That helps our reviewers.
- For the INF-4821 reference — can you surface the mitigation plan summary (bullet list) in the attestation PDF so auditors can see steps taken and rollback plan?
- We would like the DocuSign-signed attestation if possible.

Michael from AuditCo is on copy to accept the packet for our SOC2 folder. If you can send the DocuSign link we can sign and close the loop.

Best,
Alice

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finserv.com>, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 31 Aug 2025 16:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: Keystone VM evidence and remediation attestation

Hi Alice / Michael — following up with the finalized language. We attached an updated PDF (cve-closure-attestation-keystone-2025-08.pdf) that includes:
- Explicit sentence: "Redwood Inference confirms no evidence of active exploitation related to CVE-2025-3397 or CVE-2025-7841 was found after log and EDR review during the stated windows."
- INF-4821 mitigation summary (bullet list of steps and rollback plan).
- Signature block for an authorized security officer.

DocuSign link to the attestation: https://docusign.example/sign/KB-2025-08-keystone-attest
HubSpot record for our correspondence: https://hubspot.example/record/FIN-4821

If you want raw logs for forensics, we require an incoming transfer agreement (standard evidence transfer NDA). If the SIG intake requires anything else (e.g., additional CSV columns or artifact TTL), flag it and we'll iterate.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference
